\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{افاقہ} (ifāqā)}{افاقہ (ifāqā)}]{\ur{افاقہ} (ifāqā) — an easing (of an illness); relief}

\label{lesson:UR-C481-ifaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to lay (someone) down, then the Urdu for to cover someone up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{افاقہ}}
\textbf{\ur{افاقہ}} — \emph{ifāqā} — \textquotedblleft{}an easing (of an illness); relief\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دوا} \ur{سے} \ur{مریض} \ur{کو} \ur{افاقہ} \ur{ہوا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{davā se marīz ko ifāqā huā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The medicine brought the patient some relief.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{افاقہ}} (\emph{ifāqā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ifāqa}, \textquotedblleft{}recovering, coming to oneself\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ifāqā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ifāqā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{davā se marīz ko ifāqā huā.} — The medicine brought the patient some relief.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to lay (someone) down, then the Urdu for to cover someone up, then say \emph{ifāqā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{افاقہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An easing (of an illness); relief\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بحال} (bahāl)}{بحال (bahāl)}]{\ur{بحال} (bahāl) — restored; back to normal}

\label{lesson:UR-C481-bahal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to cover someone up, then the Urdu for an easing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بحال}}
\textbf{\ur{بحال}} — \emph{bahāl} — \textquotedblleft{}restored; back to normal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ایک} \ur{ہفتے} \ur{بعد} \ur{اس} \ur{کی} \ur{صحت} \ur{بحال} \ur{ہو} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ek hafte bād us kī sehat bahāl ho gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A week later her health was back to normal.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بحال}} (\emph{bahāl}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{bahāl}, \textquotedblleft{}restored\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{ba}, \textquotedblleft{}to, in\textquotedblright{}, and Arabic \emph{ḥāl}, \textquotedblleft{}state\textquotedblright{}: back in its proper state.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مالش} \ur{کرنا} (mālish karnā)}{مالش کرنا (mālish karnā)}]{\ur{مالش} \ur{کرنا} (mālish karnā) — to massage}

\label{lesson:UR-C481-malish-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an easing, then the Urdu for restored.

\textbf{\ur{مالش} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{mālish karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to massage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ammī ne dādī kī kamar kī mālish kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mum massaged my grandmother's back.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{سر} \ur{کی} \ur{مالش} \ur{کی}, \emph{us ne sar kī mālish kī}.

\textbf{\ur{مالش} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{mālish karnā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{مالش}}, usually traced to Persian \emph{mālish}, \textquotedblleft{}rubbing\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دبانا} (dabānā)}{دبانا (dabānā)}]{\ur{دبانا} (dabānā) — to press gently}

\label{lesson:UR-C481-dabana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for restored, then the Urdu for to massage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دبانا}}
\textbf{\ur{دبانا}} — \emph{dabānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to press gently\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بیٹی} \ur{نے} \ur{ابو} \ur{کا} \ur{سر} \ur{دبایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{beṭī ne abbū kā sar dabāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The daughter gently pressed her father's head.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کندھا} \ur{دبایا}, \emph{us ne kandhā dabāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دبانا}} (\emph{dabānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{dābnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to press\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{dabb}, \textquotedblleft{}press\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 6173).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سینکنا} (seṅknā)}{سینکنا (seṅknā)}]{\ur{سینکنا} (seṅknā) — to warm a sore place; to toast}

\label{lesson:UR-C481-senkna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to massage, then the Urdu for to press gently.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سینکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سینکنا}} — \emph{seṅknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to warm a sore place; to toast\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دادی} \ur{گرم} \ur{پانی} \ur{سے} \ur{گھٹنا} \ur{سینکتی} \ur{ہیں۔}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādī garm pānī se ghuṭnā seṅktī haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کمر} \ur{سینکی}, \emph{us ne kamar seṅkī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سینکنا}} (\emph{seṅknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{sẽknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to warm, to foment, to toast\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{sēkk}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 13581).
